evidence_boundary: Public-source documentary synthesis only. No raw sample-level, household, health, private-well, personal or operational records were imported.

sources.title: Realisation of the Right to Water in Georgia — Special Report of the Public Defender of Georgia
sources.provenance_note: Prepared by the Office of the Public Defender with assistance from UN/UNDP and other partners; the report states that its contents are the sole responsibility of the author.

sources.title: State control and monitoring trends of drinking water quality in Georgia
locators: PDF pp. 1-5; abstract and Methods state secondary analysis of NFA 2020-2023 monitoring data; p. 3 reports 49.5% in 2023
sources.provenance_note: The article's formal peer-review procedure was not independently verified from accessible journal policy pages.

sources.title: Summary reports in accordance with Article 7 of the Protocol on Water and Health — Georgia
sources.publisher: Government of Georgia (submitted through UNECE/WHO reporting system)
locators: PDF p. 1 (Submitted 2025-04-01); p. 16 (all-standard non-compliance narrative); pp. 54-56 (sample-source response blank and E. coli table)
sources.provenance_note: This is a Government of Georgia submission, not an independent UNECE/WHO survey. The report states Georgia had not ratified the Protocol and did not set Protocol target indicators for 2022-2024.

findings.statement: The Public Defender's 2025 report states that lack of information about drinking-water quality among residents was one of the main challenges observed during its monitoring visits.
findings.limitation: This is an oversight finding from the report's monitoring work, not a nationally representative prevalence estimate.

findings.statement: The Public Defender reports visits to five regions, 35 villages and 15 municipalities, interviews with residents and requests for written municipal information; some responses were missing, incomplete or differed from residents' accounts.
findings.limitation: The report does not establish a probability sample of all Georgian settlements; the observations must not be generalized as a national percentage.

findings.statement: The Public Defender recommends a unified platform/database for understandable public information on drinking-water quality-control results and supplementary dissemination mechanisms beyond the online platform.
findings.limitation: A recommendation is not evidence that such a platform is absent today or that implementation has not occurred after the report.

findings.statement: The JECM 2025 article describes its work as a secondary hygienic analysis of National Food Agency monitoring data for 2020-2023 and reports 49.5% non-compliance among monitoring samples in 2023.
findings.limitation: The article does not provide raw sample-level records or a complete sample-selection design; formal peer-review status was not independently verified.

findings.statement: The Government of Georgia's report submitted through the UNECE/WHO reporting system reports 44.5% broad drinking-water standard non-compliance for 2023 and 40.3% for 2024; its E. coli table is a separate indicator context.
findings.limitation: The 2023 44.5% figure is not numerically reconciled with JECM's 49.5%; the submitted report does not provide enough sample-frame/denominator detail to resolve the five-percentage-point difference.

findings.statement: A high-value AquaSignal opportunity is a provenance-aware public-information and accessibility layer that makes authorized monitoring results easier to find and understand, rather than an independent national water-safety score.
findings.locator: Synthesis of the cited report findings and indicator limitations
findings.limitation: The inference identifies a research opportunity; it does not measure current service performance or prove that a new platform would improve health outcomes.

findings.statement: If authorized results are published with clear sample context, indicator definitions, freshness, correction history and non-digital access routes, residents and local service partners may understand official water-quality information more reliably.
findings.locator: Proposed testable hypothesis derived from PDF p. 54 recommendations
findings.limitation: Requires usability, accessibility and comprehension testing with approved participants; no effect is established.

findings.statement: A bilingual, low-bandwidth public result page with printable municipal notices, phone/contact alternatives and a correction request path may be a practical interface for an authority-owned disclosure service.
findings.limitation: No prototype usability test, authority approval, data-sharing agreement or operational integration has been performed.

design_requirements.requirement: Keep potable-network compliance, groundwater-source monitoring, surface-water monitoring and bottled-water testing in distinct data domains.
design_requirements.rationale: Different matrices, sampling frames and authorities cannot be combined into one indicator without a validated mapping.
design_requirements.privacy_boundary: No individual private-well records or owner data.

design_requirements.requirement: Every public result must carry source authority, sample frame, sampling date, point type, analyte, value, unit, method, laboratory/accreditation status, QA flags, applicable standard/version, denominator where relevant, publication date and revision history.
design_requirements.rationale: A percentage without denominator and sample context cannot support reliable comparison or local operational inference.
design_requirements.privacy_boundary: Use only authority-approved location precision and suppress small cells.

design_requirements.requirement: Represent missing, delayed, withdrawn and not-yet-published results as explicit states; never convert missing data into a safe/normal status.
design_requirements.rationale: Absence of a published result is not evidence of compliant water.
design_requirements.privacy_boundary: Do not infer or expose a household's water source from missing records.

design_requirements.requirement: The responsible authority owns result publication, interpretation, corrections and any public notice; NOEMA only validates provenance/completeness and renders approved information.
design_requirements.rationale: Avoids duplicate warning authority and unauthorized health advice.
design_requirements.privacy_boundary: No autonomous declaration of safe/unsafe water.

design_requirements.requirement: Provide complementary dissemination options such as accessible web pages, printable notices and authority-approved phone/community channels.
design_requirements.rationale: An online-only interface may exclude people with limited connectivity, accessibility needs or language barriers.
design_requirements.privacy_boundary: No individual device tracking or behavioural advertising.

design_requirements.requirement: Retain immutable source references and correction/version events, with public aggregates only.
design_requirements.rationale: Users need to distinguish the latest approved result from a superseded or corrected result.
design_requirements.privacy_boundary: No personal contact details, exact private-well coordinates or individual health data.

limitations: Documentary synthesis only; no field survey, interviews or municipality-level verification were conducted by NOEMA.
The Public Defender's municipal visits are not a nationally representative probability sample.
JECM's 49.5% and the Government submission's 44.5% broad 2023 indicators remain unreconciled; neither should be used as a current local risk score.
No raw NFA, NEA, utility or laboratory sample-level data was obtained or imported.
No current public-information platform inventory, accessibility audit or user-comprehension baseline was completed.
The proposed disclosure layer is an architecture hypothesis; no operational prototype or authority integration is deployed.
